correctness.rationale: Conditioning on the immunization time gives the exact success probability as the Laplace transform \(\mathbb E[e^{-hT}]\). Strict Jensen convexity proves the fixed-time extremum for every nonnegative integrable waiting law with mean \(T_*\). The exponential and fixed-time flux and stock formulas follow from competing risks and Little-style steady residence accounting. Boundary behavior is explicit: equality occurs only at deterministic waiting, while all stated strict comparisons assume \(hT_*>0\).

value.rationale: The source itself identifies comparison of its ODE and fixed-time vaccination mechanisms as problematic. Mean matching supplies a canonical calibration, and the theorem shows the remaining difference is not neutral: deterministic waiting is the worst case for immunization-before-infection among all mean-matched laws, while the common Markov ODE systematically overstates successful immunization. The result is structural, exact, and directly informs interpretation or calibration of the source models rather than being an arbitrary parameter exercise.
